6.3 You must ensure that your Participants receive appropriate health and safety induction, training and supervision, and that systems are in place for checking this, both within your own organisation and at any of your supply chain partners.

6.4 You must complete risk assessments, instruct, inform and train your Participants on the control measures identified. There are specific risk assessments for young people, pregnant workers, lone workers and employees who are engaged in manual handling activities. In addition, there may be specific risks flagged by the PTWA such as Participants who have restrictions imposed on them by probation for example, they are not allowed to use IT due to probation conditions in the short or long term etc.

6.5 DWP may visit you and your supply chain partners for a variety of reasons. When doing so, we will, in the course of our duties, adopt an ‘awareness’ approach to health and safety. In doing this we will not be conducting a health and safety inspection, nor will we be able to offer advice on whether something is safe or not. Instead, we will approach this from the position of any layperson.

6.6 However, if we do spot something on which we require assurance or clarification we will raise this with you or your supply chain partner’s representative at the location we are visiting. If it is subsequently decided that the issue raised is one that requires follow up action, this will be arranged with you through your Performance Manager (PM).

Accidents

Arrangements for managing and reporting accidents

6.7 In reporting and managing accidents, which involve a Confident Futures Participant, you and your supply chain partners may wish to consider using similar or the same procedures as you use for existing employees. However, these procedures should ensure that:

immediate action is taken to ensure the safety of your Participants and prevent reoccurrence

all accidents, including minor incidents, are recorded in your accident book

all accidents covered by the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations 2013 (RIDDOR) are reported to the appropriate enforcing authority

an investigation is carried out to assess whether any changes should be made to the workplace or procedures following the accident or incident

Risk Assessment Control Measures are reviewed and, if necessary, revised to ensure their effectiveness and that they remain suitable and sufficient

6.8 In doing this, you will wish to take into account the full range of factors relating to the incident including, for example, whether:

your Participant had received appropriate Health and Safety awareness and instruction and that they understood the implications

the activities undertaken by your Participant at the time of the accident were required as part of Confident Futures

supervision was adequate

appropriate clothing and equipment were being used

the work environment was organised in a safe manner

6.9 Should your Participant need to make a claim to an industrial injuries benefit you should direct them to the Industrial Injuries Disablement Benefit (IIDB) site on gov.uk for an application form and contact details for the IIDB contact Centre.

Unacceptable behaviour

6.10 Participants on Confident Futures have a responsibility to behave in an appropriate manner just as they would if they were in employment. You should explain what constitutes appropriate behaviour as part of the induction.

6.11 Where cases of misconduct or unacceptable behaviour by your Participants arise, you should immediately deal with it in the most appropriate manner. Where the inappropriate behaviour is of a minor nature, such as an initial refusal to co-operate, you should aim to handle the issue internally in the first instance. It is important that you keep an audit trail of all misconduct communications and record the situation, date and method of communication used to address this in case this is needed for investigation at a later date.

6.12 If an incident is more serious or there is a pattern of unacceptable behaviour, for example, damage to property or continued refusal to co-operate with reasonable requests, you should notify the PTWA or other nominated contact point.

6.13 You are required to notify the PTWA of all incidents of unacceptable behaviour that involve your Participants. We consider the following as examples of unacceptable behaviour:

violence

verbal abuse, including that of a sexual or racist nature

threats, which are implied or otherwise;

intimidation

sexual innuendo

harassment

unwelcome attention

attempted or actual assaults

inappropriate use of the internet or provider’s IT system

This list is not exhaustive.

6.14 When notifying DWP of an incident you should complete the UCCF02 form and select urgent 2-way call and send to the appropriate designated Jobcentre Inbox. You should then contact your Jobcentre Plus SPoC and advise that you have submitted the form and require an urgent call.

Exclusions from provider premises

6.15 Only in extreme circumstances should you request that your Participant be excluded from your site(s). Before any such request, you are required to attempt to manage your Participant within your business, moving them to an alternative site where available and necessary. As a last resort you may request that your Participant is excluded from your site(s).

Note: This is not exclusion from Confident Futures, only from your site(s).

6.16 If your Participant’s behaviour is consistently unacceptable and other methods of engaging or issuing verbal or written warnings prove ineffectual, you may wish to request that your Participant is excluded from your premises. The situation must be one of genuine risk to staff and not just because your Participant is difficult, and you must supply evidence about why exclusion is appropriate.

Additional Provision delivered as part of Jobcentre Plus Offer: A Participant on Confident Futures cannot usually be referred to provision that is delivered as part of Jobcentre Plus Offer. This includes Sector Based Work Academy Programme (SWAP) which are not compatible with Confident Futures

a work experience opportunity subsidised or funded by you, or through an arrangement that you have with an employer or training partner (outside of the official SWAPs initiative) would be compatible with Confident Futures and could be considered for a Participant

non-DWP Contracted Provision: Provision offered by Local Authorities, Charities, the Private sector (this list is not exhaustive) may be compatible with Confident Futures. It is the responsibility of the provider to check the eligibility and suitability criteria of the specific provision or support being considered

Chapter 3b: Residency Tests and Participants with EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS) status

Participants and Residency Tests

3.75 You may be informed through a change of circumstances notification UCCF01, or by your Participant that they have an issue with their residency. If your Participant informs you of this, you may wish to contact the PTWA through a UCCF02 notification form to request a 2 or 3-way call to seek confirmation.

EUSS Status and Habitual Residence Test Decisions

3.76 Should your Participant fail the Habitual Residency Test (HRT), their Universal Credit claim will close. They will however remain on Confident Futures if they wish to do so and have the right to work and reside in the UK. Passing the Universal Credit HRT is not a requirement for continued participation where the individual retains the right to work and reside in the UK.

3.77 Should your Participant make a new claim for Universal Credit, they will remain a Participant until a new HRT is undertaken. Should your Participant pass the new HRT, the Participant will continue on the Confident Futures Programme. Should your Participant fail the new HRT but retains the right to work and right to reside in the UK, they may continue on Confident Futures if they wish to do so.

3.78 Should a Participant appeal an HRT decision that is subsequently overturned, their Universal Credit claim may be reinstated, they will be able to continue on the Confident Futures Programme.

3.79 You should be aware that the HRT used for Universal Credit assesses whether an individual is habitually resident in the UK and, where applicable, whether they have a qualifying right to reside for benefit purposes. A person’s right to work and general right to reside is determined by their immigration status, which the Home Office is responsible for. Support may continue to be provided to Participants who do not satisfy the HRT, but who hold Settled Status, Pre-Settled Status or a valid Certificate of Application under the EU Settlement Scheme. Providers should check and record the Participant’s right to work and general right to reside where appropriate.

Participants requiring permission to enter or remain in the UK

3.80 If a Participant’s leave to enter or remain in the UK expires whilst they are on Confident Futures, Jobcentre Plus will confirm the Participant’s immigration status via a UCCF01 Change of Circumstances form which will also provide the actions for you to take in all circumstances.

3.81 If Jobcentre Plus confirm that a Participant is an overstayer because they no longer hold valid leave and do not benefit from section 3C leave, they do not have permission to work in the UK. The Participant must be exited from Confident Futures using the appropriate Leaver Code.

3.82 If Jobcentre Plus confirm that the Participant made a valid application to the Home Office before their existing leave expired, their leave may be automatically extended under section 3C of the Immigration Act 1971 pending the outcome of that application. The Participant remains eligible for Confident Futures while they continue to hold valid leave. If leave is subsequently refused and no further entitlement to remain exists, they must be excited from Confident Futures using the appropriate Leaver Code.

Chapter 3c: Supporting Participants with complex needs and additional support needs on Confident Futures

Supporting Participants with complex needs

3.83 Complex needs may be defined as difficult personal circumstances or life events. They may be permanent or temporary in nature and the degree to which they affect a Participant will vary from one to another.

3.84 There is no prescriptive list of complex needs which DWP can supply. Some Participants will have obvious physical conditions which mean they need extra support or that adjustments are required to enable them to fully engage and access support fully. Other Participants may have conditions that are less obvious. You should refer to your organisations policies and guidance for further information regarding identification.

3.85 Examples of complex needs may include (but are not limited to):

learning disability

recent care leaver

drug or alcohol dependency

unable to read or write

homelessness

3.86 As a minimum you are expected to assess your Participants during every interaction, supported by information from Jobcentre Plus to identify complex needs and provide a support offer that is tailored to meet these needs where appropriate. This includes the activities you agree to support them to find and retain work.

3.186 All breaks in support and discussions concerning them must be recorded in the Support Plan.

Chapter 3h: In-Work Support (IWS) on Confident Futures

3.187 IWS will be provided to Participants who move into employment. For those Participants entering work, and with their consent, you should, complete an Employment Support Plan (ESP) and issue it to the employer within 10 working days of the Participant entering Employment or self-employment.

3.188 IWS will be in place for either the remainder of the Participants time on the programme (up to 365 days from their start date) or until the they no longer require it.

3.189 In the rare event where a Participant does not agree to an ESP being produced, you must ensure this decision is clearly documented, dated, and formally recorded in their Support Plan. Supporting evidence should also be retained to support compliance and assurance activities. If the Participant wants to remain on the programme you should continue to provide tailored IWS to them and continue to update their Support Plan.

3.190 If a Participant moves into employment, remind the Participant to notify their PTWA as per Chapter 3e: Change of Circumstances while on Confident Futures. They may decide they do not require IWS, and they can choose to end their participation in the programme at this point. Refer to Chapter 4: Leaving Confident Futures and Chapter 8: Using the Provider Referral and Payment (PRaP) System for Confident Futures for action to take for completers in this scenario.

Note: You should not request the Participant to notify the PTWA if they are not in receipt of Universal Credit.

3.191 You will be responsible for the design of the ESP which must set out the support you will give to the Participant and the employer during the IWS period, for the duration of the programme (up to 365 calendar days), to help the Participant sustain employment. It will also include the Participant’s support needs from the employer after you are no longer involved, after the period of IWS. The ESP should contain as a minimum:

a description of the IWS you are providing to the Participant

any actions required of the Participant in relation to the IWS

all Non-Confident Futures Activities

3.192 You must provide tailored IWS to both the Participant and the employer to help the Participant stay in work, except where the Participant has stated they do not require it. The IWS should be provided by the same Dedicated Adviser, and to the same frequency and intensity as during the pre-employment support phase.

3.193 The same level of support will be expected for those Participants who choose to become self-employed. It is not intended that you would act in a small business advisor capacity, rather you should continue to support the Participant with on-going management of their barriers to work as you would with an employed Participant. You should signpost the Participant towards agencies that can support them with appropriate business advice, including helping the Participant to access the Access to Work (AtW) provision.

3.194 Support for each Participant must include, but is not limited to:

maintaining frequency of contact (at least once every 4 calendar weeks) with Participant, with any additional contact as required

where appropriate, the Participant being accompanied to the workplace by the Dedicated Adviser, and the Dedicated Adviser supporting the Participant in meetings with the Participant’s line manager and colleagues

on-going engagement with the Participant’s wider sustainable support network (both formal and informal networks)

practical actions, for example socialising and integration in the work environment, journey planning, pre-start visits for familiarisation, establishing a buddy in the workplace

facilitating any reasonable adjustments required and where appropriate, ensuring Access to Work (AtW) assistance is in place from the from the start of employment

3.195 The ESP must be updated when the Participant enters employment or self-employment and at least every 4 calendar weeks throughout IWS. Where Participant has stated they do not want an ESP, you should update the Support Plan.

3.196 Check the possible impact on the Participant’s welfare benefits of any paid employment undertaken and ensure these are understood by the Participant.

Confident Futures employer support offer

3.197 You will be expected to have and to build strong links to national and local employers, helping to build disability confidence and to increase the capacity and sustainability of employers including Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) to recruit and retain disabled people.

3.198 You must provide a full employer support offer focussed on working with the employer so that the employer can continue to support the Participant in work after the provision has ended. The employer support offer will include meeting with employers and their staff and encouraging employers to find champions/advocates within their workplace. This will also involve up-skilling employers and developing a support network that will continue to work together to meet the Participant’s needs and help them to sustain employment.

3.199 You have a role in developing the confidence of the employers you work with in the delivery of the Provision to accommodate disabled people in their workplace and to understand the principles of “Disability Confident”. This includes increasing an employer’s disability awareness and capability. You will need to ensure that employers are able to continue to support each Participant with their support network and AtW where appropriate once the delivery of IWS on Confident Futures ends.

Local tailoring and stakeholder engagement
